intended_object: The (i, j) coordinate function x_ij in the coordinate ring O(SL_n) = K[x_ij, det⁻¹]/(det − 1) over a commutative ring K, i.e. the (i, j) entry of the universal determinant-one matrix. This comes from the docstring and from how the module uses it (`polynomialEquiv_variable`, `determinant_entry`).
explanation:
The library builds `GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.CoordinateRing K n` as `Localization.Away (det X)`, where `X` is the generic matrix `Matrix.mvPolynomialX n n K`. `GeneralLinearCoordinateRing.matrix K n` is the image of `X` in that localization, so it is the universal invertible matrix. `SpecialLinearCoordinateRing.CoordinateRing` is the quotient of this ring by the ideal (det − 1), and `quotient` is the quotient map. `entry K n i j` sends the (i, j) entry of the universal GL matrix into that quotient, which is exactly the coordinate function x_ij on SL_n.

The library's own results confirm this reading:
- `determinant_entry` shows that the matrix of these entries has determinant 1.
- `polynomialEquiv_variable` shows that `entry` corresponds to the class of `X (i, j)` in the polynomial presentation K[x_ij]/(det − 1).

The setting is already the natural one: any commutative ring K and any finite index type n with decidable equality. The only restriction is that n and K must live in the same universe, which is harmless. Mathlib has no coordinate ring of SL_n, so there is no counterpart to cite.
